title: Cabinet-chart diffusion with an explicit world-context escape path
coverage_gap: D_5 has 3 LL and 2 HH episodes and no crossed position/yaw cells; yaw extrapolation is roughly +/-35 degrees rather than the observed -6.17 to +7.63 degrees. A raw-state policy can associate cabinet translation, yaw and phase. Near-constant yaw cosine also has a very small support standard deviation.
reusable_regularity: Hand-to-handle corrections and the handle-to-goal displacement can be described in the observed cabinet yaw frame. Use a direct, nonlearned 53-dimensional chart per observation and express translation actions in that same yaw frame. No fitted action rule or waypoint is added. Two rotation-matrix columns replace xyzw quaternions, removing antipodal ambiguity without losing physical attitude. Fixed metric scales avoid amplification of nearly constant support coordinates.
dependencies_preserved: World hand, handle and goal positions, their previous positions, and cabinet sin/cos remain explicit. This is not full SE(2) invariance: fixed robot orientation, world action cube, table height and reachability can still matter.

Current and native-previous hand/handle relative vectors, full physical handle attitude, gripper apertures and causal finite differences are retained. The two whole input observations are encoded separately.

Cabinet placement and yaw plus handle pose retain the available cabinet/panel obstacle dependence. No unobserved collision geometry or hidden hinge state is queried. Object2 channels are omitted only because the schema declares them absent zeros.

evidence_refs.detail: Only the five listed support episodes; image-and-numeric evidence bundle.

expected_failure_signature: If gripper/panel contact is not yaw-equivariant, initial approach may improve yet the hand can slip or collide during pulling, especially at the two yaw extremes.
The world escape path may still memorize the correlated training layouts: a persistent C gap despite canonical relative features falsifies the intended decorrelation benefit.
Without explicit phase supervision, lowering may occur too early or pulling may begin before contact. This should appear as a stationary handle with a moving hand rather than steady opening.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41]; no additional runtime fields
required_runtime_fields.normalization: Use raw values with contact scale 0.1m, span/world scale 0.5m, one-step motion scale 0.01m, unit attitude/yaw/aperture and 0.1 aperture-difference scale; common normalized history is deliberately replaced.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Encode action xyz as Rz(cabinet_yaw_at_chunk_start)^T times native xyz. Decode with Rz, retaining native 0.01m control units. All 16 steps use the same causal frame. Gripper is unchanged. No local clipping or rescaling; executor alone clips the decoded world cube and executes four steps.

support_fit: None. Metric scales are representation choices, not estimates from other data.
change_summary: Initial scientific design: deterministic cabinet chart, sign-invariant attitude, direct geometric conditioning, orthogonal action mapping; factory U-Net and action epsilon loss are unchanged. No performance feedback used.
